title: Sunda Kingdom
capsule: The Sunda Kingdom was a Hindu Sundanese polity ruling western Java from its establishment in 669 CE, succeeding the Taruma Kingdom, with its capital eventually at Pakuan Pajajaran near present-day Bogor. The reign of Sri Baduga Maharaja (1482–1521), traditionally identified with the legendary Prabu Siliwangi, marked the kingdom's golden age: it controlled the pepper trade through Sunda Kalapa (modern Jakarta) and maintained diplomatic contact with the Portuguese, who erected a padrão stone at Sunda Kalapa in 1522. The city fell to the Demak-allied commander Fatahillah in 1527, breaking the Portuguese alliance and severing Sunda's access to the sea. Persistent pressure from the rising Sultanate of Banten finally destroyed Pakuan Pajajaran and extinguished the kingdom in 1579.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Sunda's history is attested through Sundanese inscriptions (notably the Kebon Kopi II inscription of 932), Portuguese records, and Javanese chronicles, but territorial boundaries — particularly the eastern frontier with Majapahit and later Demak — are imprecisely defined.
